sections.content:
Topic 1. Verb to be (am / is / are)
Complete the sentences with am, is or are.
	•	I ___ a student.
	•	My sister ___ 25 years old.
	•	They ___ from Italy.
	•	We ___ very happy today.
	•	This ___ my new phone.
Topic 2. Subject pronouns and possessive adjectives
Choose the correct option.
	•	(He / His) is my brother.
	•	This is (I / my) house.
	•	(They / Their) are teachers.
	•	She loves (she / her) dog.
	•	(We / Our) parents are at home.
Topic 3. Articles (a / an / the)
Complete the sentences with a, an or the.
	•	I have ___ apple.
	•	She is ___ doctor.
	•	This is ___ interesting book.
	•	I live in ___ small apartment.
	•	___ sun is very bright today.
Topic 4. Singular and plural nouns
Write the plural form of each noun.
	•	Child
	•	Box
	•	City
	•	Woman
	•	Potato
Topic 5. This / That / These / Those
Choose the correct word.
	•	___ is my pen here in my hand. (This / Those)
	•	___ are my shoes over there. (That / Those)
	•	___ is your house across the street. (This / That)
	•	___ are my friends standing next to me. (These / That)
	•	___ is a beautiful picture on the wall over there. (This / That)
Topic 6. Have got / Has got
Complete the sentences with have got or has got.
	•	She ___ a new car.
	•	I ___ two brothers.
	•	They ___ a big house.
	•	My father ___ blue eyes.
	•	We ___ a lot of books.
Topic 7. Present Simple — affirmative
Put the verbs in brackets into the Present Simple.
	•	She ___ (work) in a hospital.
	•	I ___ (play) football every weekend.
	•	My father ___ (drive) to work.
	•	They ___ (live) in London.
	•	Tom ___ (study) English every day.
Topic 8. Present Simple — negative
Rewrite the sentences in the negative form.
	•	She likes coffee.
	•	They work on Sundays.
	•	He plays tennis.
	•	I speak French.
	•	We watch TV every evening.
Topic 9. Present Simple — questions
Make questions using Do or Does.
	•	You like chocolate.
	•	She work in a bank.
	•	They live in Spain.
	•	He play the guitar.
	•	Your parents speak English.
Topic 10. Adverbs of frequency
Put the adverb in the correct position.
	•	I am late. (never)
	•	She drinks coffee. (always)
	•	They go to the gym. (usually)
	•	He is tired. (sometimes)
	•	We watch films. (often)
Topic 11. Present Continuous
Put the verbs in brackets into the Present Continuous.
	•	She ___ (read) a book now.
	•	They ___ (play) football at the moment.
	•	I ___ (cook) dinner right now.
	•	He ___ (watch) TV.
	•	We ___ (study) English today.
Topic 12. There is / There are
Complete the sentences with There is or There are.
	•	___ a cat in the garden.
	•	___ three bedrooms in my house.
	•	___ a supermarket near here.
	•	___ five students in the classroom.
	•	___ a book on the table.
Topic 13. Prepositions of place
Complete with in, on, under, behind or next to.
	•	The book is ___ the table.
	•	The cat is ___ the bed.
	•	The supermarket is ___ the bank.
	•	The children are ___ the classroom.
	•	The garden is ___ the house.
Topic 14. Prepositions of time
Complete with at, on or in.
	•	I wake up ___ 7 o’clock.
	•	My birthday is ___ July.
	•	We have English classes ___ Monday.
	•	I go to bed ___ night.
	•	She was born ___ 2005.
Topic 15. Can / Can’t
Complete with can or can’t.
	•	Birds ___ fly.
	•	Fish ___ walk.
	•	I ___ speak English.
	•	A baby ___ drive a car.
	•	My brother ___ swim very well.
Topic 16. Imperatives
Complete the sentences using the correct imperative form of the verbs in brackets.
	•	___ the door, please. (open)
	•	___ in the classroom. (not / run)
	•	___ your homework. (do)
	•	___ so loudly. (not / speak)
	•	___ careful! (be)
Topic 17. Countable and uncountable nouns
Write C (countable) or U (uncountable).
	•	Water
	•	Apple
	•	Rice
	•	Chair
	•	Milk
Topic 18. Some / Any
Complete with some or any.
	•	I have ___ friends in London.
	•	There isn’t ___ milk in the fridge.
	•	Would you like ___ tea?
	•	Are there ___ eggs?
	•	We need ___ apples.
Topic 19. Possessive ’s
Rewrite the sentences using possessive ’s.
	•	The bag of Sarah.
	•	The car of my father.
	•	The room of my brother.
	•	The toys of the children.
	•	The house of my grandparents.
Topic 20. Basic conjunctions (and / but / because)
Complete with and, but or because.
	•	I like tea ___ coffee.
	•	She is tired ___ she is happy.
	•	He stays at home ___ he is sick.
	•	My brother is tall ___ I am short.
	•	I study English ___ I want to travel.

sections.title: PART 3. READING — A1
sections.content:
Read each text carefully. Then answer all five questions. Use complete sentences whenever possible.
Reading 1. My Daily Routine
Daily life
My name is Anna. I am 22 years old, and I live in a small apartment in London. I work in a supermarket. Every morning, I get up at seven o’clock. I have breakfast with my sister. I usually eat eggs and toast and drink a cup of tea.
I go to work by bus. My work starts at nine o’clock and finishes at five. After work, I sometimes meet my friends. We go to a café or walk in the park. In the evening, I cook dinner, watch TV and read a book. I usually go to bed at eleven o’clock.
Questions
	•	How old is Anna?
	•	Where does she live?
	•	What does she eat for breakfast?
	•	How does she go to work?
	•	What does she usually do in the evening?
Reading 2. My Family
Family
I have a small family. There are four people in my family: my mother, my father, my younger brother and me.
My mother is a teacher. She works at a school near our house. My father is a doctor. He works in a hospital. My brother is 12 years old. He likes football and computer games.
We live in a big house. There are three bedrooms, two bathrooms, a kitchen and a living room. On Sundays, we usually have lunch together. My mother cooks delicious food, and my father makes a salad. I help them clean the kitchen.
Questions
	•	How many people are there in the family?
	•	What does the mother do?
	•	Where does the father work?
	•	What does the brother like?
	•	What does the family usually do on Sundays?
Reading 3. A Weekend Trip
Travel
Last weekend, David and his friends went to a small village near the mountains. They left the city on Saturday morning. The weather was sunny and warm.
They stayed in a small hotel. There was a beautiful garden behind the hotel. In the morning, they had breakfast at a café. Then they walked in the mountains and took many photos.
In the evening, they went to a restaurant. David ate chicken and rice, and his friend ordered fish. They returned home on Sunday afternoon. They were tired but very happy.
Questions
	•	Where did David and his friends go?
	•	When did they leave the city?
	•	What was the weather like?
	•	What did they do in the mountains?
	•	When did they return home?
Reading 4. My Favourite Hobby
Hobbies
My name is Mark, and my favourite hobby is photography. I have a good camera, and I take photos every weekend.
I like taking photos of nature, animals and buildings. My favourite place is the city park because there are many beautiful flowers and trees.
Sometimes I go to the park with my sister. She likes drawing, so she brings her notebook and pencils. I take photos while she draws pictures.
We often spend two or three hours there. Photography makes me happy because I can remember special moments.
Questions
	•	What is Mark’s favourite hobby?
	•	When does he take photos?
	•	What does he like taking photos of?
	•	What does his sister do in the park?
	•	Why does Mark like photography?
Reading 5. A Day at the Supermarket
Shopping
Today is Saturday. Emma and her mother are at the supermarket. They need food for the week.
First, they buy some vegetables: tomatoes, potatoes, carrots and onions. Then they go to the fruit section. Emma chooses apples, bananas and oranges.
Her mother also buys milk, cheese, bread and eggs. Emma wants some chocolate, but her mother says they have enough sweets at home.
At the checkout, they pay for everything. They put the shopping in their bags and go home. Emma helps her mother prepare lunch.
Questions
	•	What day is it?
	•	Why are Emma and her mother at the supermarket?
	•	Which vegetables do they buy?
	•	What does Emma want to buy?
	•	What does Emma do when they get home?

	•	They (played / were playing) football when it started to rain.
	•	While I (walked / was walking) home, I saw an accident.
	•	He (read / was reading) a book when his mother entered the room.

	•	We ___ (watch) a film tonight.

Topic 9. Present Continuous for future arrangements

	•	We ___ (have) dinner with our parents tonight.
	•	They ___ (visit) the museum on Saturday.
	•	He ___ (see) the doctor tomorrow morning.
Topic 10. Comparative adjectives

	•	My house is ___ (big) than yours.
	•	This exercise is ___ (easy) than the previous one.
	•	My brother is ___ (tall) than me.
	•	Today is ___ (hot) than yesterday.
	•	This book is ___ (interesting) than that one.
Topic 11. Superlative adjectives
Complete the sentences using the superlative form.
	•	Mount Everest is the ___ (high) mountain in the world.
	•	She is the ___ (young) person in our family.
	•	This is the ___ (good) restaurant in town.
	•	It was the ___ (bad) day of my life.
	•	February is the ___ (short) month of the year.
Topic 12. Countable and uncountable nouns — much / many / a lot of
Complete with much, many or a lot of.
	•	How ___ water do you drink every day?
	•	How ___ students are there in your class?
	•	I have ___ friends in my city.
	•	There isn’t ___ sugar in the kitchen.
	•	We don’t have ___ time.
Topic 13. A few / A little / Few / Little
Complete with a few, a little, few or little.
	•	I have ___ friends at university.
	•	There is ___ milk in the fridge.
	•	We have very ___ time, so hurry up.
	•	She has ___ books about history.
	•	There is very ___ sugar left.
Topic 14. Some / Any / No
Complete with some, any or no.
	•	There are ___ apples in the basket.
	•	I don’t have ___ money with me.
	•	There is ___ milk in the fridge. We need to buy some.
	•	Would you like ___ coffee?
	•	There are ___ students in the classroom. It is empty.
Topic 15. Must / Mustn’t / Have to / Don’t have to
Choose the correct modal or expression.
	•	You ___ wear a seat belt in a car.
	•	You ___ smoke in the hospital.
	•	I ___ get up early tomorrow because I have an exam.
	•	You ___ bring food. We have enough.
	•	Students ___ do their homework.
Topic 16. Should / Shouldn’t
Complete with should or shouldn’t.
	•	You ___ eat more vegetables.
	•	He ___ go to bed so late.
	•	You ___ see a doctor if you feel ill.
	•	They ___ spend all their money.
	•	I think you ___ study more for the exam.
Topic 17. Adverbs of manner
Change the adjectives into adverbs and complete the sentences.
	•	She speaks English ___ (good).
	•	He drives very ___ (careful).
	•	The children played ___ (happy).
	•	Please walk ___ (slow).
	•	My teacher explains everything ___ (clear).
Topic 18. Present Perfect — ever / never
Complete the sentences using the Present Perfect form.
	•	I ___ never ___ (visit) Japan.
	•	___ you ever ___ (eat) sushi?
	•	She ___ never ___ (see) snow.
	•	They ___ (travel) to France.
	•	___ he ever ___ (ride) a horse?
Topic 19. Present Perfect — just / already / yet
Complete with just, already or yet.
	•	I have ___ finished my homework.
	•	Have you eaten lunch ___?
	•	She has ___ bought a new phone.
	•	They haven’t arrived ___.
	•	We have ___ seen this film.
Topic 20. First Conditional
Complete the sentences using the correct form of the verbs.
	•	If it ___ (rain), we will stay at home.
	•	If I study hard, I ___ (pass) the exam.
	•	She will be happy if you ___ (call) her.
	•	If they don’t hurry, they ___ (miss) the bus.
	•	If you heat water to 100°C, it ___ (boil).

sections.title: PART 3. READING — A2
sections.content:
Read each text carefully. Answer all five questions after each text. Use full sentences.
Reading 1. Moving to a New City
Life experiences
Last year, Sophie moved from a small town to a large city because she found a new job there. At first, she felt nervous because she didn’t know anyone. The streets were crowded, the buildings were tall, and the city was much noisier than her hometown.
During her first week, she had some problems. She got lost twice and missed her bus one morning. However, she didn’t give up. She started using a map application and asked her colleagues for advice.
After a few months, everything became easier. Sophie made new friends, discovered interesting cafés and joined a local sports club. Now she enjoys city life and doesn’t want to move back.
Questions
	•	Why did Sophie move to a large city?
	•	How did she feel at first?
	•	What problems did she have during her first week?
	•	How did she solve her problems?
	•	Why does she enjoy living in the city now?
Reading 2. A Healthy Lifestyle
Health and lifestyle
Many people want to live a healthier life, but they don’t know where to start. A healthy lifestyle doesn’t always require expensive equipment or special food.
First, it is important to eat different kinds of food. Fruit, vegetables, fish and whole grains are good choices. Drinking enough water is also necessary.
Second, people should do physical activities regularly. Walking, cycling and swimming are excellent ways to stay active. You don’t need to exercise for several hours every day. Even a 30-minute walk can improve your health.
Finally, getting enough sleep is important. Adults usually need around seven to nine hours of sleep each night. Small changes can make a big difference over time.
Questions
	•	Does a healthy lifestyle always require expensive equipment?
	•	Which foods are mentioned as healthy choices?
	•	Name three physical activities from the text.
	•	How long can a daily walk be to help improve your health?
	•	Why is getting enough sleep important?
Reading 3. An Unforgettable Holiday
Travel and experiences
Two years ago, my family and I travelled to Turkey for our summer holiday. We stayed in a hotel near the sea. The hotel was comfortable, and there were many restaurants and shops nearby.
Every morning, we went swimming or walked along the beach. In the afternoon, we visited different places. We saw an old castle, explored a local market and tried traditional food.
One day, we decided to take a boat trip. The weather was beautiful, but suddenly the wind became stronger. The boat stopped for a short time, and everyone felt a little worried. Luckily, the captain knew what to do, and we continued our journey safely.
It was one of the best holidays I have ever had. I hope to visit Turkey again.
Questions
	•	When did the family travel to Turkey?
	•	Where was their hotel?
	•	What places did they visit?
	•	What happened during the boat trip?
	•	Why was the holiday unforgettable?
Reading 4. Learning a New Skill
Education and personal development
Daniel wanted to learn how to play the guitar for a long time. Last January, he finally decided to take guitar lessons.
At first, learning was difficult. His fingers hurt, and he couldn’t play even a simple song. Sometimes he wanted to stop, but his teacher encouraged him to continue.
Daniel practised for twenty minutes every day. He watched online videos, learned new chords and listened to different kinds of music.
After three months, he could play several songs. He was very proud of his progress. Now he plays the guitar for his friends and family.
Daniel believes that learning a new skill takes time and patience. He wants to learn the piano in the future.
Questions
	•	What skill did Daniel want to learn?
	•	When did he start taking lessons?
	•	Why was learning difficult at first?
	•	How did he practise?
	•	What does he want to learn in the future?
Reading 5. Shopping Online or in a Shop?
Shopping and technology
Today, many people prefer shopping online because it is quick and convenient. They can buy clothes, books and electronic products without leaving home. Online shops often offer special discounts, and customers can compare prices easily.
However, shopping online also has disadvantages. Sometimes products look different from their pictures. Delivery can take several days, and returning an item may be difficult.
Shopping in a physical shop has some advantages too. Customers can see, touch and try products before buying them. They can also take their purchases home immediately.
I usually prefer shopping in physical shops when I buy clothes, but I enjoy buying books online because it is more convenient.
Questions
	•	Why do many people prefer shopping online?
	•	What are two disadvantages of online shopping?
	•	What can customers do in physical shops?
	•	Why does the writer prefer buying clothes in physical shops?
	•	Which shopping method do you prefer and why?

sections.title: PART 3. READING — B1
sections.content:
Read each text carefully. Pay attention to the main ideas, details, vocabulary in context and the writer’s opinions.
Answer all five questions after each text. Use complete sentences.
Reading 1. The Importance of Stepping Outside Your Comfort Zone
Personal development
Many people prefer to stay in their comfort zone because it makes them feel safe. They follow familiar routines, spend time with people they know and avoid situations that might make them uncomfortable. Although this lifestyle can be pleasant, it may also prevent people from developing new skills and discovering their abilities.
A few years ago, Emily was afraid of speaking in public. Whenever she had to give a presentation at university, she felt extremely nervous. She often avoided participating in discussions because she was worried about making mistakes.
One day, her professor encouraged her to join a public speaking club. At first, Emily didn’t want to participate, but she decided to give it a try.
During the first meetings, she struggled to express her ideas clearly. However, she continued practising and gradually became more confident. After six months, she was able to deliver a presentation in front of more than one hundred people.
Emily realised that making mistakes was not something to be ashamed of. Instead, mistakes helped her improve.
Today, she believes that personal growth begins when people are willing to face their fears and try something new.
Questions
	•	Why do many people prefer staying in their comfort zone?
	•	What problem did Emily have at university?
	•	How did her professor encourage her?
	•	What difficulties did Emily experience at the beginning?
	•	What lesson did Emily learn from this experience?
Reading 2. How Technology Has Changed the Way We Work
Technology and work
Technology has significantly changed the modern workplace. In the past, most employees had to travel to an office every day, communicate through face-to-face meetings and complete many tasks manually.
Today, digital tools allow people to work from almost anywhere. Employees can attend online meetings, share documents and communicate with colleagues through messaging applications. As a result, remote work has become increasingly popular.
Working remotely offers several advantages. People can save time because they don’t need to travel to the office. They may also have more flexibility and spend more time with their families.
However, remote work also creates challenges. Some employees find it difficult to separate their professional and personal lives. Others feel lonely because they don’t interact with colleagues regularly.
Another important issue is communication. Online messages can sometimes cause misunderstandings because people cannot always understand the speaker’s tone or emotions.
In my opinion, technology has made work more flexible and efficient, but companies should find a balance between digital communication and personal interaction.
Questions
	•	How did people communicate at work in the past?
	•	What tools allow people to work remotely today?
	•	Mention two advantages of remote work.
	•	Why do some employees find remote work difficult?
	•	What balance does the writer believe companies should find?
Reading 3. The Problem of Plastic Pollution
Environment
Plastic is used in almost every part of modern life. People use plastic bags, bottles, food containers and packaging because these products are cheap, light and convenient.
However, plastic pollution has become a serious environmental problem. Many plastic products are used only once and then thrown away. Some of this waste ends up in rivers and oceans, where it can harm animals and damage natural ecosystems.
Sea animals sometimes mistake plastic for food. As a result, they may become sick or die. Plastic can also break down into tiny pieces called microplastics, which can enter the food chain.
Fortunately, there are several ways to reduce plastic pollution. People can use reusable shopping bags, carry their own water bottles and avoid unnecessary packaging.
Governments and businesses also have an important responsibility. They can improve recycling systems, develop environmentally friendly materials and encourage customers to make sustainable choices.
Protecting the environment requires cooperation. Individual actions may seem small, but when millions of people make better choices, the results can be significant.
Questions
	•	Why do people use plastic products so frequently?
	•	How does plastic waste harm sea animals?
	•	What are microplastics?
	•	Give two examples of how individuals can reduce plastic pollution.
	•	Why is cooperation important in protecting the environment?
Reading 4. A Career Change at Thirty
Career and education
For almost eight years, Michael worked as an accountant in a large company. His salary was good, and his colleagues were friendly. However, he gradually realised that he wasn’t satisfied with his career.
He had always been interested in technology and enjoyed solving computer problems. In his free time, he watched programming tutorials and read articles about software development.
At first, Michael was afraid to change careers. He worried that he was too old to start learning something completely new. He also had financial responsibilities and couldn’t simply leave his job.
After considering his options, he decided to study programming in the evenings. He created a weekly schedule and spent around two hours practising every day.
After a year, Michael had developed enough skills to apply for an entry-level position at a technology company. He attended several interviews before receiving an offer.
Although his new job was challenging, he felt much more motivated. He understood that changing careers required patience, effort and careful planning.
Questions
	•	How long had Michael worked as an accountant?
	•	Why was he dissatisfied with his career?
	•	What made him afraid of changing careers?
	•	How did he prepare for his new career?
	•	What did Michael learn from this experience?
Reading 5. Is Travelling Always a Good Experience?
Travel and culture
Travelling is often considered one of the best ways to learn about the world. People visit different countries to discover new cultures, try traditional food, see famous places and meet people with different backgrounds.
One of the greatest advantages of travelling is that it can change the way people think. When travellers experience unfamiliar traditions and lifestyles, they may become more open-minded and understanding.
Travelling can also help people develop practical skills. They learn how to organise their time, manage their money and solve unexpected problems. For example, missing a train in a foreign country may be stressful, but it can teach someone how to remain calm and find another solution.
Nevertheless, travelling also has disadvantages. It can be expensive, especially during popular holiday seasons. Long journeys may be tiring, and cultural differences sometimes cause misunderstandings.
Another issue is overtourism. When too many visitors arrive in one destination, local communities may experience higher prices, crowded streets and environmental damage.
I believe travelling is valuable, but tourists should behave responsibly, respect local traditions and think about the impact of their choices.
Questions
	•	Why do people travel to different countries?
	•	How can travelling change people’s attitudes?
	•	What practical skills can people develop while travelling?
	•	What problems can overtourism cause?
	•	What does the writer believe responsible tourists should do?

Topic 3. My Ideal Career and Professional Future

Topic 5. A Difficult Situation and How I Overcame It

sections.title: PART 3 — READING COMPREHENSION
sections.content:
Read each text carefully and answer the five questions that follow it. Use complete sentences where appropriate.
Reading 1: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence
Artificial intelligence has become an increasingly important part of modern society. From recommendation systems to medical research, AI technologies are changing the way people work, communicate, and make decisions.
One of the greatest advantages of AI is its ability to process enormous amounts of information in a relatively short time. In healthcare, for example, AI systems can help doctors identify patterns in medical images and detect certain diseases earlier. In business, companies use AI to analyze customer behavior and improve their services.
However, the rapid development of artificial intelligence also raises serious concerns. Some employees worry that machines will eventually replace their jobs. Others are concerned about privacy, misinformation, and the possibility that automated systems may make unfair decisions.
Experts argue that the solution is not to reject AI but to develop it responsibly. Governments, businesses, and educational institutions need to work together to establish clear regulations and prepare people for changes in the labor market.
Ultimately, artificial intelligence is neither entirely beneficial nor entirely harmful. Its impact will depend largely on how humans choose to develop and use it.
Questions
	•	What are two areas in which AI is currently being used?
	•	How can AI help doctors?
	•	What concerns do employees have about artificial intelligence?
	•	Why is cooperation between governments and businesses important?
	•	According to the text, what will determine the impact of AI on society?

Reading 2: The Importance of Work-Life Balance
In many modern workplaces, employees are expected to remain productive, meet deadlines, and respond to messages outside normal working hours. Although technology has made communication easier, it has also made it more difficult for some people to separate their professional and personal lives.
A lack of work-life balance can have serious consequences. Employees who work excessively may experience stress, exhaustion, and reduced motivation. Over time, these problems can affect not only their professional performance but also their relationships and physical well-being.
Some companies have started introducing flexible working arrangements. These include remote work, shorter working weeks, and flexible schedules. Such policies can help employees organize their time more effectively and improve job satisfaction.
Nevertheless, flexibility alone does not guarantee a healthy work-life balance. Employees also need to establish boundaries, manage their priorities, and learn when to disconnect from work.
Achieving balance is not necessarily about spending equal amounts of time on work and personal activities. Instead, it involves making sure that neither area consistently damages the other.
Questions
	•	How has technology affected the separation between professional and personal life?
	•	Name three possible consequences of excessive work.
	•	What flexible arrangements have some companies introduced?
	•	Why is flexibility alone insufficient?
	•	How does the text define a healthy work-life balance?

Reading 3: Sustainable Tourism
Tourism is an important source of income for many countries. It creates employment, supports local businesses, and allows people to discover different cultures. However, when tourist numbers increase too quickly, local communities and natural environments may suffer.
Popular destinations sometimes experience overcrowding, rising property prices, and increased pollution. In some coastal areas, excessive tourism has damaged marine ecosystems and threatened wildlife.
Sustainable tourism aims to reduce these negative effects while maintaining the economic benefits of travel. This approach encourages visitors to respect local traditions, support independent businesses, and avoid activities that harm the environment.
Governments also have an important role to play. They can limit visitor numbers in sensitive areas, invest in public transport, and introduce environmental protection policies.
Travelers can contribute by choosing responsible accommodation, reducing waste, and learning about the places they visit before arriving.
Sustainable tourism does not mean that people should stop traveling. Rather, it means recognizing that travel comes with responsibilities.
Questions
	•	What economic benefits does tourism provide?
	•	What problems can excessive tourism create?
	•	What is the main purpose of sustainable tourism?
	•	How can governments reduce the negative effects of tourism?
	•	What can individual travelers do to support sustainable tourism?

Reading 4: Why People Change Careers
Changing careers has become increasingly common. In the past, many people expected to remain in the same profession throughout their working lives. Today, however, technological developments, economic changes, and personal ambitions have encouraged more individuals to reconsider their career choices.
Some people change careers because they are dissatisfied with their current positions. Others want to pursue a long-standing interest or find work that offers greater flexibility. In certain cases, employees are forced to change professions because their industries are becoming less relevant.
Although changing careers can create new opportunities, it is rarely an easy process. Individuals may need to acquire new qualifications, gain practical experience, and accept a temporary reduction in income.
Financial planning is therefore essential. Before making a major decision, people should research the new industry, identify transferable skills, and consider the long-term consequences.
Despite the challenges, a career change can be highly rewarding. It may provide a stronger sense of purpose, improved job satisfaction, and opportunities for personal development.
Questions
	•	Why are career changes more common today?
	•	Give two reasons why someone might change careers.
	•	What difficulties can people experience during a career transition?
	•	Why is financial planning important?
	•	What are three possible benefits of changing careers?

Reading 5: The Psychology of Decision-Making
Every day, people make hundreds of decisions, ranging from simple choices about what to eat to major decisions about education, relationships, and careers. Although decision-making may appear straightforward, it is influenced by a wide range of psychological factors.
One important factor is cognitive bias. This occurs when people rely on mental shortcuts that can lead to inaccurate judgments. For example, confirmation bias makes individuals more likely to notice information that supports their existing beliefs while ignoring evidence that challenges them.
Emotions also influence decision-making. When people are anxious or under pressure, they may focus on immediate outcomes rather than considering long-term consequences. On the other hand, excessive analysis can sometimes prevent individuals from making any decision at all.
Experts recommend approaching important decisions systematically. This involves identifying the available options, gathering reliable information, considering potential consequences, and evaluating personal priorities.
However, not every decision can be made with complete certainty. Sometimes people must act despite limited information and accept that mistakes are part of the learning process.
Questions
	•	What is cognitive bias?
	•	Explain confirmation bias in your own words.
	•	How can anxiety affect decision-making?
	•	What steps do experts recommend for making important decisions?
	•	Why is it sometimes necessary to make decisions without complete certainty?
